headline: The NAD+
question.
dek: NAD+ drips and injections are sold for aging. The largest trial of a related pill went the wrong way.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Oct 31, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: Largest trial
glance.line: NOPARK, 410 people with Parkinson’s: disease scores worsened more on oral NR than placebo.

glance.label: Not approved
glance.line: NAD+, NR, glutathione, MOTS-c and Epitalon: none is FDA approved for any use.

glance.label: Banned in sport
glance.line: MOTS-c is named under S4.4.1. NAD+, NR, metformin and Epitalon are not named.

paragraphs: [[/nad|NAD+]] is a coenzyme every cell uses, and it is one of the most-sold longevity treatments. Adonis carries it through Beluga as a compounded injection and a compounded nasal spray; neither is FDA approved. The human evidence for injected NAD+ is small: one pilot study of an IV infusion in 11 healthy men, a chart review of 14 clinic clients, and two randomized trials in China that used a hospital NAD+ injection for heart disease, not aging. We found no published human study of NAD+ nasal spray.

Its relative has been tested far more. [[/nicotinamide-riboside|Nicotinamide riboside]] (NR), a form of vitamin B3 the body turns into NAD+, has been through many randomized trials by mouth. They show it raises NAD+ in the blood; effects on health have been small, mixed or absent. The largest, NOPARK, gave oral NR or placebo for 52 weeks to 410 people with early Parkinson’s disease in Norway. NR did not help: the disease score worsened 2.72 points more on NR than on placebo, and non-motor symptoms also worsened more. NR is sold as a supplement; no NR injection is FDA approved, and the one Adonis carries is compounded.

[[/metformin|Metformin]] is the approved drug in the lane, as Glucophage since 1995 and many generics, for type 2 diabetes. Use for aging is off-label. The aging evidence is small trials of aging biology and exercise in older adults; in older adults it reduced some gains from exercise. A large trial called TAME was proposed in 2016, and we found no registry record for it. Its label carries a boxed warning for lactic acidosis.

Two peptides here have less. FDA’s 2026 review found no published study in which [[/mots-c|MOTS-c]] was given to people; one trial is registered with no results. WADA names it under S4.4.1 and bans it at all times. For [[/epitalon|Epitalon]], FDA found three studies that gave it to people and none that assessed safety; most of the research comes from one St. Petersburg group. Since October 30, 2026, HHS has allowed both to be compounded under set conditions, which is enforcement discretion, not approval. Adonis does not carry either today. [[/ghk-cu|GHK-Cu]] and [[/sermorelin|sermorelin]] also sit in this lane, with no human study measuring longevity.

[[/glutathione|Glutathione]] raises a quality problem. On August 27, 2026, FDA said it knew of at least 30 patients with adverse events after IV glutathione compounded by different pharmacies from one supplier’s lot, labeled dietary supplement grade; some were hospitalized. FDA had issued a similar warning in 2019, and in October 2026 Greenwich Rx recalled glutathione injections for elevated endotoxin.

Adonis carries glutathione as a compounded injection and nasal spray; neither is FDA approved. Its human studies are few and small, mostly in Parkinson’s disease, where they did not show a clear benefit over placebo. None measured aging.

pull.quote: The glutathione was labeled as dietary supplement grade, which is not an appropriate ingredient to make injectable drugs.
